speaker: Unknown
en: And now there's a bunch of great services that host a ton of different models and they all offer text input to output.
zh: 现在有很多很棒的服务托管了大量不同的模型，它们都提供文本输入到输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so most people don't want to be competing on just offering the lowest price for every model or offering the fastest inference or things like that.
zh: 所以大多数人不想仅仅通过为每个模型提供最低价格或提供最快的推理之类的东西来竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they're really trying to think about...

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我如何更深入地进入特定类型的创作者或专业人士的工作流，这样他们除了价格之外有真正的理由留在我的平台上？

zh: 我想这就是每个人现在都在思考的主要挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's worth...

speaker: Unknown
en: probably having a point of view on that if you're starting a new company today in the generative media space.
zh: 如果你今天要在生成式媒体领域创办一家新公司，这值得对此有一个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are so many incredible creators out there who you can sell to, but also figuring out where the opportunities are because things are changing all the time is the hardest part, right?
zh: 有这么多令人难以置信的创作者你可以卖给，但同时也弄清楚机会在哪里，因为事物一直在变化，这是最难的部分，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you think the untapped opportunity is for a founder to build a defining company in this category?
zh: 你认为在这个类别中，对于想要建立一家标志性公司的创始人来说，未开发的机会在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think most of the companies in this space initially targeted like the AI native creators, you know, folks like us who were early adopters of all of these tools, who were using and sharing and posting about it, who were reachable on platforms like X and Reddit.
zh: 我是说，我认为这个领域的大多数公司最初的目标是像 AI 原生创作者，你知道，像我们这样的人，是这些工具的早期采用者，正在使用、分享和发布关于它的内容，可以在像 X 和 Reddit 这样的平台上触达到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's a massive market of other people that are largely untapped, who are less technically sophisticated, who don't know every single tool out there.
zh: 但我认为有一个巨大的其他人群市场在很大程度上未被开发，他们的技术水平不那么高，不知道外面的每一个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in some ways, that's a benefit because if you get them on your tool and you get them to have a sticky workflow there, like they're less fickle, they're less likely to turn and go to whatever they see the next day.
zh: 在某种程度上，这是一个好处，因为如果你让他们使用你的工具，并让他们在那里有一个粘性的工作流，就像他们不那么善变，他们不太可能第二天转变去做他们看到的任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a lot of opportunity in consumer that's honestly untapped, like sort of the social layer of generating and sharing stuff is still almost entirely done on the existing incumbent platforms versus, you know, creating really fun and interesting and compelling new playgrounds where consumers can make and share this sort of stuff.
zh: 我认为消费领域有很多机会实际上是未开发的，就像生成和分享内容的社会层面几乎仍然完全是在现有的 incumbent 平台上完成的，而不是，你知道，创造真正有趣和引人注目的新游乐场，让消费者可以在那里制作和分享这种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think types of content, like micro dramas are a great example where you need really specific things.
zh: 我还认为内容类型，比如微剧集就是一个很好的例子，你需要非常具体的东西。

en: Like, and I saved ideas of characters with certain voices, saved sets, like a sense of the right timing and pacing for a micro drama in particular.

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that sort of knowledge and those features are going to be different than a general video product.
zh: 就像那种知识和那些功能将与通用视频产品不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think there are also a lot of opportunities in like vertical industries, things like architecture, things like design.
zh: 然后我认为在像垂直行业也有很多机会，比如建筑，比如设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: Marketing and ad industry is huge and is just starting to adopt AI.
zh: 营销和广告行业非常庞大，并且才刚刚开始采用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think going into those markets that are not necessarily like the most AI native is an enormous opportunity right now.
zh: 所以我认为进入那些不一定是最 AI 原生的市场目前是一个巨大的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like there are so many opportunities founders could go towards.
zh: 感觉好像有太多的机会，创始人可以朝向这些方向去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I almost feel, is there going to be like a Roblox equivalent for AI micro dramas maybe?
zh: 我几乎感觉，会不会有一个像 Roblox 同等的东西用于 AI 微剧集？

speaker: Unknown
en: All of these AI tools where you can create ads in like a couple of minutes, I think it's been so interesting to see.
zh: 所有这些 AI 工具，你可以在几分钟内创建广告，我觉得看到这一点非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: We mentioned earlier around like presentations, creators have to create slide decks and partnership agreements and stuff.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And so every minute they spend on that sort of thing is a minute that they can't spend on creating content, which is generally what they like to do.

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of my takes is that AI...
zh: 所以我的观点之一是 AI……

speaker: Unknown

zh: 智能体对于个体创作者和小企业来说将特别强大，只是因为他们在时间和资源方面受到的约束要大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's going to be a massive step function improvement for them when they can spend much more of their time on their creation, their business, whatever they like to do, and less on all of this administrative and logistical type stuff.
zh: 当他们可以将更多的时间花在他们的创作、他们的业务、他们喜欢做的任何事情上，而更少地花在所有这些行政和后勤类型的事情上时，这对他们来说将是一个巨大的阶梯式改进。

zh: 我真正喜欢的是它摄取关于你的所有这些信息。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 不如每次你收到一封发票或收据的电子邮件，我就自动为你转发进去，然后进行分类，这样它就不会堵塞你的收件箱？

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.

zh: 这几乎就是我感觉我们在过去两年里一直等待的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like consumer tech intersecting AI is back.
zh: 感觉像消费科技与 AI 的交汇又回来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Consumer tech has always been, there's no opportunity.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你最兴奋看到消费领域下一步走向哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can see early signs though, just like, you know, you can see early signs of like an indie songwriter, you know, rising up in TikTok and then eventually they become a big star.
zh: 我想你能看到早期的迹象，就像，你知道，你可以看到一个独立词曲作者在 TikTok 上崛起的早期迹象，然后最终他们成为大明星。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你可以从这些产品的早期采用者那里看到未来可能是什么样子的迹象，一旦每个人都能接触到它。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we saw the first wave of a lot of that kind of stuff with like OpenClaw, honestly, and the Hermes agent where really technical people were...
zh: 我想我们看到了那种东西的第一波浪潮，老实说，就像 OpenClaw 和 Hermes 智能体，真正懂技术的人在……

speaker: Unknown
